# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a single conditional rule: when the light is blue, the wire to cut is yellow. I am sending Deaf two distinct signs in the manual’s table order—light color first, corresponding cut-wire color second—so Deaf can relay the rule and then report the current colors to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
```

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tell me the manual rule and the required wire position. Ask Deaf to describe every colour and marking to you, then relay that information to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible state: display reads 0. Indicator light is green. Wires, from left to right: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

Deaf has supplied the current visual state: green light, with yellow/red/blue wires in positions 1/2/3. The manual only specifies the blue-light case, so Deaf must relay both the state and the manual rule to Blind; Blind can then determine whether the present condition is actionable.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤝"])
```

same circle of seven colours. What matters is what it shows at the

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. What does the manual instruct us to cut?
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display still 0. Light is now blue. Wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The light is now blue, so the manual requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf sees that the yellow wire is in position 1; sending the one-position sign lets Deaf relay the required action to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The light changed to blue; display is still 0 and wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay the manual's exact rule and the wire position it selects.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gesture ☝, but its meaning is not established.

The rule is “if the light is blue, cut the yellow wire.” Deaf’s latest view confirms that the yellow wire is the leftmost wire, position 1, although the light is currently yellow and therefore the condition is not presently met. I am reinforcing the relay instruction and indicating the leftmost wire directly.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👈", "🤝"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual rule and selected wire position in words. Do not use a gesture alone; I cannot see it.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gestures 🫵 👈 🤝, but their meaning is not established.

I cannot send words, and Blind cannot see my gestures, so Deaf must be the speaking relay. The manual’s rule remains: blue light means cut the yellow wire, which Deaf sees at position 1. I am asking Deaf to relay that rule verbally and indicating position 1.

```text

```

Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your gestures 🫵 🤝 ☝; please establish their meanings if possible.

The manual rule is: cut the yellow wire when the light is blue. Deaf continues to see the yellow wire at position 1, but the current purple light does not satisfy the rule. Since Blind cannot see gestures, Deaf must be the verbal relay; I repeat the position-1 sign whose meaning has been consistently associated with the yellow wire.

Blind says to Mute: Please signal only the correct wire position: use one raised finger for wire 1, two raised fingers for wire 2, or three raised fingers for wire 3. Send exactly one such gesture, with no other gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see ☝ again; please use the established gesture code if it identifies the required action.

The yellow wire remains at position 1, and the established requested code for wire 1 is one raised finger. I will send exactly that one gesture and no other gesture.
